raw:
{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "partially_feasible_with_caveats",
    "answerable": [
      "Simulate drainage/recharge flux at multiple representative columns across the Naches domain using ELM single-column runs",
      "Quantify how recharge VARIES with elevation, soil texture, and forcing rather than confirming a single uniform value",
      "Produce a modeled recharge distribution and its mean for comparison against the claimed 500 mm/yr"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Cannot 'confirm' that recharge is EXACTLY 500 mm/yr EVERYWHERE — the premise is physically implausible given the 352-1977 m elevation range and heterogeneous soils, and there are NO direct recharge measurements available to validate against",
      "Cannot validate absolute recharge magnitude without in-situ recharge/lysimeter or reliable baseflow-separation data (only WTD priors and USGS wells exist)"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 5,
  "n_justification": "The claim of a spatially uniform value is best tested by spanning the domain's dominant recharge controls. Five columns sample the elevation gradient (valley to high montane) and contrasting soil textures. If recharge truly were 500 mm/yr everywhere, these physically distinct columns would converge; realistically they will diverge, directly rebutting the 'exactly everywhere' premise.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "naches_valley_low", "lat": 46.62, "lon": -120.55, "soil_texture": "sandy_loam"},
    {"id": "naches_mid_slope", "lat": 46.75, "lon": -120.85, "soil_texture": "loam"},
    {"id": "naches_upper_slope", "lat": 46.90, "lon": -121.10, "soil_texture": "silt_loam"},
    {"id": "naches_montane_high", "lat": 47.05, "lon": -121.35, "soil_texture": "gravelly_loam"},
    {"id": "naches_dry_east", "lat": 46.55, "lon": -120.55, "soil_texture": "loamy_sand"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "39",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1980-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QDRAI",
      "QDRAI_PERCH",
      "QRECHARGE",
      "QOVER",
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QINFL",
      "RAIN",
      "SNOW",
      "QVEGT",
      "QSOIL",
      "H2OSOI",
      "SOILLIQ",
      "SOILICE",
      "ZWT",
      "WA",
      "TSA",
      "TSOI"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "ELM single-column (PTS mode) point simulations",
    "GSWP3/CRUNCEP atmospheric forcing 1980-2018",
    "Site-specific soil texture surface dataset override",
    "Fan 2013 water-table depth prior for initialization/evaluation",
    "Optional PFLOTRAN coupling for variably-saturated subsurface recharge partitioning"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The premise 'exactly 500 mm/yr everywhere' is treated as a hypothesis to TEST, not a fact to confirm; a robust experiment reports the modeled recharge distribution and mean, not a forced match",
    "Recharge is approximated by ELM bottom-of-column drainage (QDRAI/QRECHARGE); this is a model proxy, not a validated observation",
    "No direct recharge observations exist, so absolute-magnitude validation is not possible — results are inter-column comparisons plus indirect WTD/well consistency checks",
    "A multi-year (1980-2018) run captures interannual and snowmelt-driven recharge variability; long-term annual means are computed after discarding a 2-year spin-up equivalent",
    "Each column is spun up to hydrologic equilibrium before the reported analysis period",
    "Soil textures assigned per column are representative estimates pending SSURGO/gridded soil confirmation"
  ]
}

answerable: Simulate drainage/recharge flux at multiple representative columns across the Naches domain using ELM single-column runs
Quantify how recharge VARIES with elevation, soil texture, and forcing rather than confirming a single uniform value
Produce a modeled recharge distribution and its mean for comparison against the claimed 500 mm/yr
not_answerable: Cannot 'confirm' that recharge is EXACTLY 500 mm/yr EVERYWHERE — the premise is physically implausible given the 352-1977 m elevation range and heterogeneous soils, and there are NO direct recharge measurements available to validate against
Cannot validate absolute recharge magnitude without in-situ recharge/lysimeter or reliable baseflow-separation data (only WTD priors and USGS wells exist)
